newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks plunge on tensions with Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks plunge on tensions with Turkey.

text.p: Cyprus stocks fell 1.75 percent during the week on renewed tensions with Turkey sparked by Cypriot plans to buy Russian missiles.
The CSE general index closed at 80.71 on Friday, registering a 1.44 point fall since last week's closure of 82.15 points.
Banking stocks, the strongest of the seven indices, slumped 181 points, or 1.97 percent in the four trading days this week. The market was closed on Monday for the Epiphany holiday.

On Friday Turkey threatened to strike at a missile system Cyprus has agreed to buy from Russia. Cyprus says it needs the missiles -- due to be installed next year -- for its own defence, while Ankara says they are offensive.
"The threats are 100 percent related (to the market fall)," said Nicos Severis, chairman of Sigma Severis and Athientis Securities in Nicosia.
"This is a local issue and it does have a direct impact on the country," he added.
The island has been divided since a Turkish invasion in 1974 sparked by a brief coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece.
Fully paid shares in the Bank of Cyprus closed at 336.5, slipping 7.5 cents from last week. Fully paid shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank dropped six cents, to 324.5.
The Hellenic Bank dropped 4.5 cents to 260.
Universal Savings Bank dropped one cent to 137.
Insurance stocks also declined, closing at 56.27 points from 57.79 last week.
Universal Life shares dropped 5.5 cents to 367.5. Paneuropean Insurance fully paid declined five cents to close at 118.5.

Cement producer Vassiliko closed at 160, up one cent from last week's levels. Earlier this week the island's central bank approved Italy's Italcementi ITAI.MA purchase of 13.2 million pounds ($28 million) of shares in Vassiliko.
The deal increases the Italian company's stake in Vassiliko to 33 percent of capital from the 20 percent it acquired in 1990.
Beer and wine producers Keo retreated five cents, closing at 110.5.
